note: Concept values for planning, loosely based on NASA crew-rover studies (Space Exploration Vehicle, Lunar Terrain Vehicle). Not measured or official specifications.

rovers.name: Pressurised crew rover
rovers.summary: Cabin for two, shelter from solar storms, long range. Carries the crew to the work site and back.

rovers.name: Unpressurised crew rover
rovers.summary: Open vehicle for two suited astronauts. Lighter and more agile, no shelter.

rovers.name: Helper robot
rovers.summary: Small robot that follows the astronaut with tools and samples. The simulation uses a Clearpath Jackal as a stand-in.

equipment.name: Robotic arm, heavy
equipment.use: Reaches samples on slopes the crew must not enter, lifts crates.

equipment.name: Robotic arm, light
equipment.use: Picks up small rocks and places sample tubes.

equipment.name: Core drill
equipment.use: Drills rock cores of the boxwork ridges.

equipment.name: Geology tool kit
equipment.use: Hammer, scoop, tongs, rake, as on Apollo.

equipment.name: Sample containers (box of 12)
equipment.use: Sealed, numbered containers for rock and soil.

equipment.name: Handheld spectrometer
equipment.use: Checks minerals on the spot before taking a sample.

equipment.name: Ground-penetrating radar
equipment.use: Maps layers and ice under the rover.

equipment.name: Lidar
equipment.use: 3D scan of the terrain and obstacles, as in the simulation.

equipment.name: Panoramic camera
equipment.use: Context images for the science team.

equipment.name: Radio relay
equipment.use: Keeps contact with the habitat in craters and valleys.

equipment.name: Spare oxygen tank
equipment.use: Refills a suit in the field: more time out, more margin on the way back.

equipment.name: Deployable solar panel
equipment.use: Recharges during long stops; Mars dust cuts its output.

equipment.name: Winch and tow line
equipment.use: Recovers a stuck vehicle from soft sand.
